alph1.explanation: θ vocātur “thēta”; sonat ut t aspīrātum, nōn ut Anglicum “th”.

alph2.prompt: Quō sonō pronūntiātur υ in Atticō reconstrūctō?
alph2.explanation: Υ Atticum est vōcālis anterior labializāta, sīcut Gallicum “u” vel Germānicum “ü”.

alph3.prompt: Quae litterae Graecae sunt SEMPER longae?
alph3.explanation: Η et ω semper vōcālēs longae sunt; ε et ο semper brevēs; α ι υ possunt esse utrumque.

alph4.prompt: Quōmodo sonat σ inter duās vōcālēs in Atticō Classicō?
alph4.explanation: Σ in Graecō Classicō semper est /s/ surdum.

alph5.prompt: Quid accidit litterae γ ante γ, κ, χ, vel ξ (ut in ἄγγελος)?
alph5.explanation: Ante hās litterās, γ assimilātur ad sonum nāsālem vēlārem “ng”.

alph6.explanation: Occlūsīvae aspīrātae (θ φ χ) differunt ab occlūsīvīs simplicibus (τ π κ) sonō aspīrātiōnis statim sequentis; ψ et ξ semper sunt coniūnctiōnēs duārum cōnsonantium.
alph6.exerciseInstructions: Iunge quamque litteram cum dēscrīptiōne phōneticā suā.

alph7.statement: Littera σ scrībitur ς cum est ultima littera verbī, sed sonus manet idem.
alph7.explanation: Corrēctum: sōla fōrma scrīptūrae mūtātur in fīne verbī, nōn sonus.
alph7.exerciseInstructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

alph8.statement: In pronūntiātiōne Atticā reconstrūctā, θ sonat ut Anglicum “th” in “think”.
alph8.explanation: Falsum: θ Atticum est occlūsīva aspīrāta (t+h), nōn fricātīva ut Anglicum “th”.
alph8.exerciseInstructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

alph9.statement: Alphabētum Graecum Classicum habet vīgintī quattuor litterās.
alph9.explanation: Corrēctum: XXIV litterae, post reformātiōnem Atticam annō 403 a.C. officiāliter adoptātam.
alph9.exerciseInstructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

alph10.statement: Vōcālēs ε et ο possunt esse aut brevēs aut longae, sīcut α.
alph10.explanation: Falsum: ε et ο sunt SEMPER brevēs; sōlum α, ι, υ possunt variāre longitūdine.
alph10.exerciseInstructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

eimi1.exerciseInstructions: Comple spatia cum fōrmā rēctā verbī εἰμί. (Accentūs nōn necessāriī sunt ad respōnsum probandum, sed disce eōs rēctē scrībere.)

eimi2.exerciseInstructions: Comple spatia cum fōrmā rēctā verbī εἰμί. (Accentūs nōn necessāriī sunt ad respōnsum probandum, sed disce eōs rēctē scrībere.)

eimi4.exerciseInstructions: Comple spatia cum fōrmā rēctā verbī εἰμί. (Accentūs nōn necessāriī sunt ad respōnsum probandum, sed disce eōs rēctē scrībere.)

eimi5.exerciseInstructions: Comple spatia cum fōrmā rēctā verbī εἰμί. (Accentūs nōn necessāriī sunt ad respōnsum probandum, sed disce eōs rēctē scrībere.)

eimi6.prompt: Quis cāsus post εἰμί semper adhibētur (ut praedicātum)?
eimi6.explanation: Praedicātum post εἰμί semper nōminātīvō pōnitur, sīcut post Latīnum ‘sum’.

options: ν additum fīnī ἐστί/εἰσί ante vōcālem vel pausam
eimi7.explanation: Est ν movēns additum ut hiātus vītētur et pausa signētur.

eimi8.prompt: Quōmodo dīcitur “who are you?” Graecē (cum signō interrogātiōnis rēctō)?

eimi9.explanation: χαίρετε est fōrma plūrālis salūtātiōnis χαῖρε.

eimi10.prompt: Cūr prōnōmen ἐγώ saepe omittitur ante εἰμί?
options: quia dēsinentia verbī iam persōnam indicat
quia εἰμί semper prīmam persōnam significat sine prōnōmine
eimi10.explanation: Verba Graeca, sīcut Latīna, persōnam in dēsinentiā portant; prōnōmen est optiōnāle, prō ēmphasī tantum.

eimi11.explanation: Salūtātiōnēs Graecae plērumque nōn sunt versiōnēs verbālēs Latīnārum, sed fōrmulae propriae cum sēnsū homologō.
eimi11.exerciseInstructions: Iunge quamque phrasim Graecam cum sēnsū Latīnō suō.

spir1.explanation: Spīritus asper indicat sonum /h/ pronuntiandum ante vōcālem vel diphthongum initiālem.

spir2.prompt: Super quam litteram diphthongī pōnitur spīritus (et accentus, sī adest)?
spir2.explanation: In diphthongō, signa (spīritus et accentus) super secundam vōcālem scrībuntur, ut in εἰμί vel αὐτός.

spir3.prompt: Quae littera initiālis SEMPER accipit spīritum asperum?
spir3.explanation: Omnis ρ initiālis verbī accipit spīritum asperum (ῥ), unde Latīnum “rhētor” in verbīs mūtuātīs.

options: in ūnā ex tribus ultimīs syllabīs
spir4.explanation: Accentus acūtus potest cadere in ultimā, paenultimā, vel antepaenultimā syllabā (ultimīs tribus).

options: parva iōta scrīpta sub α, η, vel ω longīs
spir5.explanation: Iōta subscrīptum (ᾳ ῃ ῳ) est parva iōta scrīpta sub vōcālī longā, vestīgium antīquae diphthongī.

pairs.right: in ūnā ex tribus ultimīs syllabīs
sōlum super vōcālem longam, in ūnā ex duābus ultimīs syllabīs
parva ι sub α, η, vel ω longīs

spir6.explanation: Quodque signum habet fūnctiōnem propriam et locum ubi lēgitimē appārēre potest.
spir6.exerciseInstructions: Iunge quodque signum cum dēscrīptiōne suā.

spir7.statement: Omnis vōcālis initiālis verbī Graecī accipit vel spīritum lēnem vel spīritum asperum.
spir7.explanation: Corrēctum: nūlla vōcālis initiālis caret utrōque signō.
spir7.exerciseInstructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

spir8.statement: Spīritus asper est mēra optiō graphica sine effectū in prōnūntiātiōne.
spir8.explanation: Falsum: spīritus asper reāliter significat sonum /h/ in prōnūntiātiōne Atticā.
spir8.exerciseInstructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

spir9.statement: Accentus circumflexus potest cadere in antepaenultimā syllabā.
spir9.explanation: Falsum: circumflexus sōlum in ultimā vel paenultimā (duābus ultimīs) cadere potest, numquam in antepaenultimā.
spir9.exerciseInstructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

spir10.statement: Initiālis ρ verbī Graecī semper accipit spīritum asperum.
spir10.explanation: Corrēctum: omne ρ initiāle habet spīritum asperum (ῥ).
spir10.exerciseInstructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.
